reading comprehension passage 1 question.question: PART 4 — READING COMPREHENSION Passage 1 — Questions 23–30 Choose the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the correct answer to each question. Question 23.What is the passage mainly about?A. Why cities should replace all waste workers with automatic collection systemsB. How festivals make public litter bins difficult to manage efficientlyC. How sensor data can improve waste collection while human judgement remains necessaryD. Why public bins should be emptied at exactly the same time each dayWrite A, B, C, or D - {#1} Question 24.The word "targeted" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to ______.A. directed toward places that need attentionB. reduced to the smallest possible numberC. controlled entirely by digital equipmentD. delayed until the following working dayWrite A, B, C, or D - {#2} Question 25.The phrase "This limitation" in paragraph 2 refers to ______.A. collection trucks still following fixed routes on some daysB. food-stall bins often filling faster during busy weekendsC. staff being able to adjust collection routes when patterns changeD. the system measuring bin fullness without identifying individual usersWrite A, B, C, or D - {#3} Question 26.According to paragraph 1, what does a sensor send to the central map?A. Names of people who use each public binB. A simple signal showing how full the bin isC. Daily instructions telling drivers which roads to avoidD. Information about the type of rubbish inside the binWrite A, B, C, or D - {#4} Question 27.Which of the following is NOT TRUE according to the passage?A. The system records personal details about people using the bins.B. Staff can change routes when some bins fill faster than others.C. Residents can still report a bin that needs attention.D. Workers may empty a bin even if sensor data suggests otherwise.Write A, B, C, or D - {#5} Question 28.Which of the following best paraphrases the final sentence of the passage?A. Smart services work best when technology completely replaces human judgement.B. City workers should make decisions without using information from sensors.C. Reliable sensor data makes regular human checks unnecessary in busy places.D. Effective smart services combine useful information with human judgement.Write A, B, C, or D - {#6} Question 29.What is the main purpose of paragraph 3?A. To argue that sensors should be removed from all public binsB. To explain system limitations and why human checks are still neededC. To compare waste-collection costs in different neighbourhoodsD. To describe how residents are taught to repair broken sensorsWrite A, B, C, or D - {#7} Question 30.What can be inferred about the planners' approach to the smart waste system?A. Planners want every waste bin emptied whenever a sensor sends data.B. The system is mainly intended to collect detailed information about residents.C. Planners value efficiency but also limit unnecessary collection of personal information.D. Human workers are expected to disappear once the sensor network expands.Write A, B, C, or D - {#8}

reading comprehension passage 2 question.question: PART 4 — READING COMPREHENSION Passage 2 — Questions 31–40 Choose the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the correct answer to each question. Question 31.The word "inclusive" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.A. too expensive for most citiesB. simple to replace when damagedC. controlled mainly by digital devicesD. suitable for many different usersWrite A, B, C, or D - {#1} Question 32.Why did the designers include printed maps and physical controls?A. To help buses move more quickly between the redesigned stopsB. To ensure the service could be used without a smartphoneC. To collect more detailed information about individual bus passengersD. To persuade residents to stop using printed travel informationWrite A, B, C, or D - {#2} Question 33.The phrase "These additions" in paragraph 2 refers to ______.A. the added maps, controls, and audio information at the stopsB. the decision to store passenger images at each bus stopC. the increase in passenger numbers during the first monthD. the problems caused by crowded buses in the city centreWrite A, B, C, or D - {#3} Question 34.Which of the following best paraphrases the design principle described in paragraph 1?A. Smart transport works well only when every passenger owns a modern phone.B. Smart services can use technology without making basic access depend on phones.C. Cities should remove digital services whenever some residents find them difficult.D. Printed information is always more reliable than digital information for passengers.Write A, B, C, or D - {#4} Question 35.What can be inferred about the designers' idea of a "smart" transport system?A. They believed the smartest system was the one using the most devices.B. They viewed smart design as technology that remained useful to different passengers.C. They expected passengers to learn the new app before using any bus.D. They regarded printed information as a temporary feature that should soon disappear.Write A, B, C, or D - {#5} Question 36.Where in paragraph 4 does the following sentence best fit?This mixed use suggested that no single information format worked best for everyone.A. [I]B. [II]C. [III]D. [IV]Write A, B, C, or D - {#6} Question 37.What is the main purpose of paragraph 4?A. To compare Eastview's transport habits with those of nearby citiesB. To report trial results and practical issues that still needed attentionC. To describe how engineers manufactured the electronic displays for the stopsD. To explain why buses were chosen instead of trains for the projectWrite A, B, C, or D - {#7} Question 38.Which of the following is NOT supported by the passage?A. Some passengers checked the real-time displays instead of relying only on the app.B. Designers provided non-digital ways to obtain basic travel information.C. The system stored images showing the identities of individual passengers.D. The city adjusted several features after practical problems appeared.Write A, B, C, or D - {#8} Question 39.Which of the following best summarises the passage?A. Smart bus stops succeed only when most passengers regularly use mobile apps.B. Eastview's trial failed because printed information could not work with smart technology.C. Smart transport works better when digital convenience is combined with accessible alternatives.D. Cities can improve transport simply by adding more digital equipment to each stop.Write A, B, C, or D - {#9} Question 40.Which of the following is the best title for the passage?A. Why Printed Maps Still Control City TransportB. Smart Stops That Work for More PeopleC. Building Faster Roads for Tomorrow's BusesD. How One App Replaced Every Bus StopWrite A, B, C, or D - {#10}

passage completionquestions 13 17read th.question: PART 2 — PASSAGE COMPLETIONQuestions 13–17Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank from 13 to 17. GRANDMA’S MID-AUTUMN LANTERNS When Mrs Hoa was a child, her family made paper lanterns for the Mid-Autumn Festival every year. Her father cut thin pieces of bamboo, while her mother prepared coloured paper. (13) ______. The children carried the finished lanterns around the village on the night of the festival. After Mrs Hoa moved to the city, she continued the tradition with her own children. At first, they found the work difficult because they had never used bamboo in this way. (14) ______. After several attempts, each child was able to make a simple star-shaped lantern. As the children grew older, they became busy with their studies. The family began buying plastic lanterns instead, and the paper-lantern tradition gradually stopped. (15) ______. Several years later, Mrs Hoa’s oldest daughter had a child of her own. She asked her mother to show her how to make the lanterns again. (16) ______. Soon, three generations of the family were working together around the same table. The new lanterns were not perfect, but they had a special meaning for the family. Mrs Hoa’s grandchildren now look forward to making them every year. (17) ______.Question 13A. The family usually bought all their lanterns from a shop near the village.B. Her parents kept the bamboo in a locked room until the festival ended.C. Mrs Hoa and her brothers helped attach the paper to the bamboo frames.D. The children preferred playing indoors instead of joining the celebration.Write A, B, C, or D – {#1}Question 14A. Mrs Hoa showed them each step and allowed them to practise slowly.B. The children decided that paper lanterns were no longer worth making.C. Her neighbours asked the family to use plastic instead of coloured paper.D. Mrs Hoa completed every lantern herself and did not let the children help.Write A, B, C, or D – {#2}Question 15A. The children sold their old schoolbooks to buy more bamboo.B. The family began celebrating a completely different festival.C. Mrs Hoa opened a shop that sold lanterns throughout the year.D. Mrs Hoa worried that her grandchildren might never learn how to make one.Write A, B, C, or D – {#3}Question 16A. The family realised that the festival had already ended several weeks earlier.B. Mrs Hoa brought out her old tools and began explaining the process.C. The children chose to watch television while Mrs Hoa worked alone.D. Her daughter bought several factory-made lanterns for the lesson.Write A, B, C, or D – {#4}Question 17A. They believe plastic lanterns should replace all handmade ones.B. The family now avoids talking about how festivals were celebrated in the past.C. By passing down the skill, the family has brought an old tradition back to life.D. Mrs Hoa’s grandchildren think the lanterns have no connection with their family.Write A, B, C, or D – {#5}

She has replaced the traditional ingredients with artificial colours.B. She cooks all five colours together instead of using separate pots.C. She prepares the natural colours before the main cooking day.D. She asks Mrs Hien to complete the difficult stages alone.Write A, B, C, or D – {#2}Question 33The phrase “This change” in paragraph 3 refers to ______.A. preparing the natural colours the night beforeB. buying all the family’s rice at the marketC. cooking the rice over a traditional wood fireD. growing and collecting ingredients at homeWrite A, B, C, or D – {#3}Question 34Why could Lan’s notebook not contain every exact instruction?A. Her grandmother wanted to keep part of the recipe secret.B. Lan stopped writing when the kitchen became full of smoke.C. The family used different ingredients for each Tet celebration.D. Some decisions depended on the condition of the rice itself.Write A, B, C, or D – {#4}Question 35What can be inferred about Lan’s experience last Tet?A. She decided that written recipes were unnecessary for young cooks.B. She learned the process more quickly by working without any guidance.C. Direct participation helped her understand her grandmother’s advice.D. Modern equipment prevented her from learning the traditional skills.Write A, B, C, or D – {#5}Question 36In which paragraph does the writer describe a change that saves preparation time?A. Paragraph 2B. Paragraph 3C. Paragraph 4D. Paragraph 5Write A, B, C, or D – {#6}Question 37What is the main purpose of paragraphs 4 and 5?A. To show how Lan developed understanding through observation and practiceB. To explain why Mrs Hien refused to answer Lan’s cooking questionsC. To compare the meanings of the five colours used in the dishD. To describe how Lan replaced experience with written measurementsWrite A, B, C, or D – {#7}Question 38Which of the following is NOT supported by the passage?A. Mrs Hien’s family formerly cooked the rice over a wood fire.B. Lan’s mother still follows the dish’s basic traditional recipe.C. Lan’s family now grows every ingredient used in the dish.D. Different generations share responsibility for preparing the dish.Write A, B, C, or D – {#8}Question 39Which of the following best summarises the passage?A. Lan’s family preserves tradition by refusing to alter any old cooking method.B. A family maintains a traditional dish while allowing practical methods to change.C. Written instructions have replaced experience in preparing a Tet dish.D. Modern equipment has made traditional family knowledge unnecessary.Write A, B, C, or D – {#9}Question 40Which of the following is the best title for the passage?A. Five Natural Colours and Their Traditional MeaningsB. How Modern Equipment Replaced an Old Cooking MethodC. The Difficulties of Preparing Food Before TetD. Learning a Family Tradition Through Shared PracticeWrite A, B, C, or D – {#10}

SMALL CHANGES WHEN YOU SHOP You do not need to change everything at once to shop more responsibly. Start by choosing products with less (1) {#1}, such as fruit sold without an extra plastic wrapper. Our shop cares (2) {#2} reducing unnecessary waste. Clean cardboard boxes are available near the checkout, so customers can carry their purchases without taking a new plastic bag. If you already have a suitable bag or box, bring it with you. These habits help (3) {#3} natural resources, including the water and trees used to produce paper products. Use available materials (4) {#4} rather than collecting more than you need. Some customers keep a folded shopping bag beside their front door, (5) {#5} makes it easier to remember the bag before leaving home. Some products still need protective packaging. (6) {#6}, we cannot remove every wrapper immediately. However, checking what you need and reusing what you already have are useful first steps.

passage completion questions 13 17 read.question: PART 2 — PASSAGE COMPLETION Questions 13–17 Read the following passage and choose the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. This report examines unnecessary electricity and water use at a community language centre. It proposes practical improvements to the way its rooms and restrooms are managed. (13) ______. Two problems need attention. Lights sometimes remain on after the last class has finished, while several taps continue dripping after use. These habits and faults waste resources without helping anyone. The centre should consider how its rooms are used before choosing new equipment. The choice between simple reminders and automatic lighting depends (14) ______. Some actions can begin immediately. The leaking taps should be repaired, and teachers should check the lights before leaving an empty classroom. (15) ______. These measures could reduce waste without changing the building’s layout. No automatic devices have been purchased yet. Automatic lights may offer another solution if reminders are not enough. Suitable devices could switch lights off when a room is empty. (16) ______. The centre would therefore still need a separate plan for checking and repairing its taps. The proposals should be introduced in a sensible order. Simple repairs and clear responsibilities can address current problems, while more expensive equipment can be considered later. The centre should also check whether its chosen measures are working. (17) ______. Question 13.A. Its main purpose is to compare language courses offered in different towns.B. It focuses on changes that staff and visitors can make without rebuilding the centre.C. It presents the results of automatic devices already installed throughout the building.D. Its main purpose is to explain why the centre needs more classrooms.Write A, B, C, or D - {#1} Question 14.A. for how often each room is usedB. at how often each room is usedC. to how often each room is usedD. on how often each room is usedWrite A, B, C, or D - {#2} Question 15.A. Staff can use a checklist to record electricity already saved by the automatic devices.B. Teachers should wait for the new lighting before checking whether classrooms are empty.C. The centre should focus only on classrooms and postpone repairs to the leaking taps.D. Staff can also place a short resource-saving checklist beside the exit.Write A, B, C, or D - {#3} Question 16.A. They would prevent water from running after taps are used, but would not affect classroom lights.B. They would warn staff about lights left on, but would require someone to switch them off.C. They would address lights left on in empty rooms, but they would not repair leaking taps.D. They would reduce lighting waste and stop tap leaks, so separate water checks would be unnecessary.Write A, B, C, or D - {#4} Question 17.A. We therefore recommend starting with repairs and clear reminders, then considering automatic lighting if necessary.B. We therefore recommend delaying all action until every visitor agrees to the purchase of automatic lighting.C. We therefore conclude that the proposed changes have already eliminated electricity and water waste completely.D. We therefore recommend rebuilding the restrooms before taking any steps to repair the existing taps.Write A, B, C, or D - {#5}

language in functional texts questions 1.question: PART 1 — LANGUAGE IN FUNCTIONAL TEXTS Questions 1–6 Read the following shopping guide and choose the best answer to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. SMALL CHANGES WHEN YOU SHOP You do not need to change everything at once to shop more responsibly. Start by choosing products with less (1) [Blank 1] , such as fruit sold without an extra plastic wrapper. Our shop cares (2) [Blank 2] reducing unnecessary waste. Clean cardboard boxes are available near the checkout, so customers can carry their purchases without taking a new plastic bag. If you already have a suitable bag or box, bring it with you. These habits help (3) [Blank 3] natural resources, including the water and trees used to produce paper products. Use available materials (4) [Blank 4] rather than collecting more than you need. Some customers keep a folded shopping bag beside their front door, (5) [Blank 5] makes it easier to remember the bag before leaving home. Some products still need protective packaging. (6) [Blank 6] , we cannot remove every wrapper immediately. However, checking what you need and reusing what you already have are useful first steps.📋BẢNG LỰA CHỌN CÁC Ô TRỐNG (CLOZE OPTIONS):Ô (1):A.compostB.equipmentC.leftoversD.packagingÔ (2):A.toB.atC.aboutD.withÔ (3):A.measureB.saveC.deliverD.displayÔ (4):A.efficientlyB.efficientC.efficiencyD.inefficientÔ (5):A.whatB.whoC.whichD.thatÔ (6):A.SimilarlyB.For exampleC.HoweverD.Therefore

language in functional texts questions 7.question: PART 1 — LANGUAGE IN FUNCTIONAL TEXTS Questions 7–12 Read the following notice and choose the best answer to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. GREENER VISITS TO THE SPORTS CENTRE Please help us use water and electricity responsibly. After using an exercise room, remember to (7) [Blank 7] the lights if nobody remains inside. Visitors who want a bottle designed for repeated use should bring a (8) [Blank 8] water bottle. Drinking water is available free of charge beside reception, so there is no need to buy bottled water during every visit. We refill a large drinking-water jug each morning, (9) [Blank 9] . Please take only the water you need and leave the area clean for the next person. Our volunteers are preparing signs to raise (10) [Blank 10] awareness. The signs will explain simple actions, including switching off unnecessary lights and reporting water leaks. To prepare (11) [Blank 11] next month's Green Day, the centre will also display leaflets about resource-saving habits. Report leaking taps to reception (12) [Blank 12] they can be repaired. Choose (1) [Blank 1] decorations that are strong enough to be stored and used at future events. Whether this plan succeeds will depend (2) [Blank 2] careful preparation. Think about the (4) [Blank 4] effects of each choice, including the rubbish left after the celebration. Volunteers will photograph how the decorations fit together before taking them down, (5) [Blank 5] will make setting them up next year easier. passage completion questions 13 17 read.question: PART 2 — PASSAGE COMPLETION Questions 13–17 Read the following passage and choose the letter A, B, C, or D to indicate the option that best fits each numbered blank. Twenty years ago, Hillcrest was a village outside the city. Most homes stood along a narrow road, while the nearest secondary school and hospital were several kilometres away. (13) ______. Reaching either facility involved a long walk followed by a bus ride. Hillcrest is now part of the expanding city. Since 2015, (14) ______. These developments have attracted families seeking larger homes outside the crowded centre. However, many adults still work in central districts, so they travel towards the city each morning. The main road has become busier. A direct bus now connects Hillcrest with the hospital, but its first departure is at nine. Morning appointments there begin at eight. (15) ______. For residents without cars, the new connection therefore has a practical limitation despite removing the need to change buses. A report also describes population trends. Between 2000 and 2020, the urban share of the region’s population rose from 30 to 45 per cent. Over the same period, the rural share fell from 70 to 55 per cent. In other words, (16) ______. These percentages describe how the population was distributed; they do not, by themselves, tell readers how many people lived in either area. Hillcrest’s development needs to be assessed through residents’ routines. For those with the earliest hospital appointments, (17) ______. Evaluating urban development involves checking how new services fit the needs of the people using them. Question 13.A. Residents could usually reach both facilities without leaving their own streetB. Residents had to travel beyond their neighbourhood to use these essential servicesC. Residents had to change buses between the school and the nearby hospitalD. Residents lived farther from the school than they did from the hospitalWrite A, B, C, or D - {#1} Question 14.A. many new housing estates will spread along the main roadB. many new housing estates have spread along the main roadC. many new housing estates had spread along the main road by 2012D. many new housing estates spread along the main road in 2010Write A, B, C, or D - {#2} Question 15.A. The first bus arrives before patients need to attend their earliest appointmentsB. The new route requires patients to change buses before reaching the hospitalC. The hospital starts seeing patients after the first bus leaves the villageD. The service starts too late for patients attending the earliest hospital appointmentsWrite A, B, C, or D - {#3} Question 16.A. the urban share gained fifteen percentage points, while the rural share lost fifteenB. the urban share reached fifteen per cent, while the rural share remained unchangedC. both shares increased by fifteen percentage points over the same reporting periodD. the rural population lost fifteen thousand people, while the urban population gained fifteenWrite A, B, C, or D - {#4} Question 17.A. providing a later return bus would solve their difficulty getting there on timeB. building another bus stop would remove the need to change the departure timeC. introducing an earlier departure would address the difficulty described in the reportD. increasing the number of seats would allow the first bus to arrive earlierWrite A, B, C, or D - {#5}
